Gauteng Health in Flames [6237]

By: Joy Summers | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Confirming what doctors at Charlotte Maxeke hospital have suspected, a leaked police forensic report shows it was arson that started the devastating fire.

Unique Selling Point:
A leaked forensic report confirming arson, a tour of the burned stores and a top doctor speaks out


Summary:
According to a recent forensic report, the devastating fire at Charlotte Maxeke was an act of arson. Doctors who work at the hospital have long suspected exactly that – now the police report confirms it.
The fire originated in the store room about a week after a stock take listed R46 million rands worth of stock including millions of rands of gloves. But doctors who we spoke to say that their suspicions arose because at the time of the fire when there was supposedly such an abundance of medical items, they were battling to get supplies and had to get them from outside the hospital. They suggest that the fire was started to hide the fact that the stock take was not an accurate reflection of the supplies. But these doctors are nervous to speak out after whistleblower Babita Deokoran was murdered. Nevertheless head of internal medicine, Professor Adam Mohamed will tell the story of the hell that healthcare workers and patients have gone through as a result of the fire. How units like obstetrics and Psychiatry have really struggled over the last 18 months. Now things are starting to turnaround but not really because of the department of health- their response has been appalling. Its thanks to the Development bank, Gift of the givers and the solidarity fund that the hospital is being rebuilt, but its not going to be quick. But the fire at this hospital is just one in a long line of disasters, graft and death at Gauteng Health.


Further information:
RUNNING THE GAUNTLET
Meanwhile parking and security are a nightmare. Doctors tell of parking chaos, and walking for miles to get to work. They have had their cars stolen, and been mugged on their way to work. Many have left ,says Professor Adam Mohamed, either for private practice or overseas.

The doctors speak of a humanitarian crisis, as people with no voice died in their homes as one of the biggest public health facilities on the continent, reeled from the effects of the blaze.

Gauteng Health is on fire and at times quite literally as section 27’s Sasha Stevenson delivered shows in a searing presentation of how disaster seems to court Gauteng Health. From the days of Brian Hlonwane whose friend allegedly won tenders worth R1.2 billion rand between 2006 and 2010. Hlongwane only resigned under pressure but was elected to the provincial ANC PEC even after Section 27 made the SIU report on his malfeasance public.

Then came the Life Esidemeni tragedy – described by Deputy Chief Justice Dikgang Moseneke as “ a harrowing account of the death, torture and disappearance of utterly vulnerable mental health care users, in the care of an admittedly delinquent provincial government”

Then in 2018 a blaze in the upper floors of Gauteng health destroyed legal documents.
But it didn’t end there, as the Covid pandemic hit, Gauteng health placed orders for PPE at a cost of more than R500 million rand above market related prices.

Then two fires in 2021 hit Gauteng Health. First the fire in April at Charlotte Maxeke and another also PPE related in Carletonville that destroyed R16.5 million rands worth of equipment which was being stored for the AngloGold Ashanti Hospital and R3.8 million worth of PPE.

In between the blazes the hero health workers kept going to work. People like Dr Tim De Maayer who went public when he couldn’t take it anymore and made the devastating statement that “Children are dying and the horrendous conditions in our public hospitals are contributing to their deaths.” For his trouble, he was almost fired and only under pressure, was he able to keep his job. Now Doctors have their heads down and are loathe to speak out. Hardly surprising when whistleblowing regarding Gauteng Health can get you assassinated. Doctors whisper Babita Deokoran’s name in hushed tones and apologize for their absence of courage to speak out.

Carte Blanche speaks to Professor Adam Mohamed, goes on a tour of the burnt hospital and asks pertinent questions of the Department of health and their response to the blaze and takes our viewers through the SAPS forensic report on the fire. We also speak to Mark Heywood formally of Section 27.

Final script Gauteng Health in Flames for TX Sunday 20th November 2022 FACT CHECKED

Vo 1
Frequent fires, a decade of malfeasance, an assassination of a whistle-blower- Is Gauteng Health a crime scene where perpetrators easily walk free?

Health activist Mark Heywood has spent a decade exposing the dark side of this R57 billion rand department

Mark Heywood
There is a mafia that is operating, a politically connected criminal mafia is exploiting this healthcare system and its vulnerability to theft

Vo 2
Fires ignite, documents are lost – in 2018 a fire burned scores of records of the Life Esidemeni tragedy in which 141 psychiatric patients died

The blaze also claimed the lives of 3 City firemen inside the bank of Lisbon building where Gauteng health kept its records

Four years later and still the reports on what happened, have not been released, despite promises to do so, by the provincial government

Fade to Black

Vo 3
From 2020 Gauteng health officials spent billions on irregular PPE contracts – and half a billion rand on this place, a now abandoned Covid hospital on Johannesburg's west rand

Adam Mohamed
Where was the thinking you are putting up a hospital for Covid 100 kilometres from where the rest of the population is staying

Vo 4
Professor Adam Mohammed is head of internal medicine at Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg Academic hospital. He remembers doctors battling to get basic medical supplies

Adam Mohamed
I went to that hospital and most of the doctors said no please stop what you are doing. Let’s cut our losses and not continue. It continued!

VO 5
Then in February 2021 Carletonville hospital’s storeroom was set alight and R20 million rands of stock was destroyed.

Fire up sound

Vo 6
But the Carletonville fire was just a curtain raiser. On 16th April 2021 the storeroom at Johannesburg’s Charlotte Maxeke hospital became yet another crime scene

LINK
There was chaos and black smoke everywhere -the heat was so intense an entire floor collapsed, it was so searing, the visors of the firefighters were melting

Vo 7
And as the fire raged Professor Mohamed was on the frontlines

Professor Adam Mohamed
It was a nightmare, got to the hospital and absolute chaos. We moved over 900 patients in under 36 hours out of that hospital. It was sad how we treated those patients like cattle but in a panic situation, we did what we needed to do.

Vo 8
Then this year, a second fire. Three fires within months couldn’t be coincidence. Then Mark leaked this police forensic report into the fire at Charlotte Maxeke. Completed more than a year ago, it found the first inferno was arson.

Mark Heywood
Some people cynically set a hospital alight knowing we were in the middle of a life threatening pandemic, shocking, and as crude and horrible and hard to imagine as that, but that is the truth!

Vo 9
Before the fire, the hospital was treating 150 000 out patients a year. Overnight wards were shut down and medical services suspended.

Jennifer had aggressive breast cancer. She was one of thousands relying on Charlotte Maxeke for treatment. After a delay she was sent to Chris Hani Baragwanath in Soweto

Bongani
And you enter Bara?
Jennifer
It was chaos! They were just queues and queues and queues and queues of patients. So many patients needed help.

V0 10
Afraid of reprisals Jennifer only wants us to use first name. She says she wasn’t just fighting the cancer, she was fighting Gauteng health to get treatment

Jennifer
The first chemo itself was actually done down the passageway in plastic chairs with everybody sharing one drip stand. But I suppose they managed to treat the patients that way.

VO 11
The hospital was damaged extensively, and it needed the Gauteng government to move quickly. But it didn’t.

Professor Adam Mohamed
The first 12 months was lies, lies, lies, we going to get the hospital fixed. Nothing happened
Bongani
When you say there have been lies – is it about a lack of a plan?
Adam
Lies such as you come and tell me you have a plan we appointing tenders, yet you haven’t allocated a budget

VO 12
When setting out on this story we were determined to get an official response, so we asked the new MEC for Gauteng Health and Wellness, Nomantu Nkomo-Ralehoko. But she has refused to discuss the fire with us, and referred us to the Premier’s office who wouldn’t entertain our questions either

Mark Heywood
The Gauteng Department of Infrastructure was meant to be responsible for the repairs, the premier issued a special proclamation to take away that responsibility from the Infrastructure department and give it to health – but the health department didn’t have the capacity, so the health department asked the Development bank to take responsibility. I mean it’s a story of our time tragically
Bongani
A tragedy of errors?
Mark
You would say a comedy of errors...but a tragedy because people have died

Thato Up sound
With inflammatory breast cancer treatment has to be frequent

VO 13
Thato Moncho was about to start radiation for aggressive breast cancer when the fire happened. During the delay her cancer returned. Now she has become a cancer educator

Thato Moncho
I tried to ask them to book me. They still say no the hospital is closed, it can't open, the premier says no the hospital is opening next week, no the president is visiting the hospital, no it's ready to open


VO 14
Thato has endured two long years of chemo, we had hoped to interview her but she cancelled saying she was too sick to speak

Mark Heywood
I would not be surprised if a lot more people have died in the aftermath of the fire than died in the life Esidimeni case

VO 15
By December 2021 Professor Mohamed was so frustrated by the delays, he wrote an open letter to the president

Adam Mohamed
We actually took a step, sorry we want to come back, even if the building is going to fall on us, but we needed to save patients and that is what we did.

VO 16
But that selflessness came at a price. Thousands of parking bays were destroyed, and as construction lagged, cars were stolen and doctors and nurses taking the long walk to work were sometimes mugged.

Yet R40 million rand is spent on security here

Professor Adam Mohamed
We have ongoing theft in our hospital – we have a second security company appointed. We have not tied up all the loose ends, we are still bleeding. When Copper piping, electrical piping is being stolen, and pipes were stolen that was being used by patients for oxygen

V0 17
And astonishingly there have been 7 fires at Gauteng hospitals including the two at Charlotte Maxeke

LINK
Who burns down a hospital? And if indeed if it was arson wouldn’t you want to throw the book at whoever was responsible

VO 18
Doctors told Carte Blanche they couldn’t get supplies, yet a stocktake at the time lists a huge inventory. The report also finds contradictory evidence from witnesses – yet the investigation has gone cold, and it was Mark himself who had to give the premier’s office a copy of the forensic report

Mark
The Gauteng Health dept claimed not to have that report so if they are to be believed, the SAPS sat with this report for a year and a couple of months, passed it on to nobody, didn’t ask internally why no investigation was going on, and the premier and the minister of health told lies, because they told the country that it was a priority and it was being actively investigating to get to the bottom of what was going on! Clearly it wasn’t!

Up sound CPR

V0 19
Perhaps that is why the new MEC and the new Premier refused to speak to us.
How can anyone explain this travesty, all the while doctors still battle massive patient backlogs in Gauteng

Up sound counting

And it's surely far easier reviving a rubber doll, and doing media junkets- than urgently fixing destruction wrought by arsonists

Bongani
Gauteng health is clearly ablaze can we put the fire out?
Mark
We could if there was a will. The rot is very deep. It needs to be someone who is willing to cut the cancer right out of the system – if you are not willing to do that then we can’t save it

Vo 20
Or do we just to accept that criminals who set fire to hospitals can burn them down and simply walk away?

THE END

PROMO ONE 11 SECONDS
A devastating fire at Johannesburg’s Charlotte Maxeke hospital left patients and doctors reeling. A forensic report found arson. But why is no-one investigating?


PROMO TWO 21 seconds
Vo
Surely a deliberate fire that closed down our second largest hospital should be a priority investigation?
Mark
Some people cynically set a hospital alight knowing we were in the middle of a life threatening pandemic
VO
But not the police, not the premiers office nor Gauteng health will even speak about it

PROMO THREE
Doctors battle at Charlotte Maxeke while officials bungle after a fire closes the hospital for months

Professor Adam Mohamed
lies, lies, lies, we going to get the hospital fixed. Nothing happened no matter all the meetings

Mark Heywood
I would not be surprised if a lot more people have died in the aftermath of the fire than in the life Esidimeni case







Eighteen months ago a fire engulfed parts of Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg Academic Hospital in Gauteng. Over 900 patients had to be moved urgently and crucial medical services came to a grinding halt. Many of the 150 000 outpatients who had relied on the hospital had to wait months for treatment. Doctors pleaded with bungling officials to fix the hospital as a matter of urgency. Then this year a forensic report was leaked that found the fire was an act of arson. But the fire at Charlotte Maxeke, is just one in a long line of disasters, graft and death at Gauteng Health. Carte Blanche investigates.

Nothing happened no matter all the meetings Mark Heywood I would not be surprised if a lot more people have died in the aftermath of the fire than in the life Esidimeni case Eighteen months ago a fire engulfed parts of Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg Academic Hospital in Gauteng. Over 900 patients had to be moved urgently and crucial medical services came to a grinding halt. Many of the 150 000 outpatients who had relied on the hospital had to wait months for treatment. Doctors pleaded with bungling officials to fix the hospital as a matter of urgency. Then this year a forensic report was leaked that found the fire was an act of arson. But the fire at Charlotte Maxeke, is just one in a long line of disasters, graft and death at Gauteng Health. Carte Blanche investigates.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Confirming what doctors at Charlotte Maxeke hospital have suspected, a leaked police forensic report shows it was arson that started the devastating fire.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: A leaked forensic report confirming arson, a tour of the burned stores and a top doctor speaks out
metadata.Summary: According to a recent forensic report, the devastating fire at Charlotte Maxeke was an act of arson. Doctors who work at the hospital have long suspected exactly that – now the police report confirms it. The fire originated in the store room about a week after a stock take listed R46 million rands worth of stock including millions of rands of gloves. But doctors who we spoke to say that their suspicions arose because at the time of the fire when there was supposedly such an abundance of medical items, they were battling to get supplies and had to get them from outside the hospital. They suggest that the fire was started to hide the fact that the stock take was not an accurate reflection of the supplies. But these doctors are nervous to speak out after whistleblower Babita Deokoran was murdered. Nevertheless head of internal medicine, Professor Adam Mohamed will tell the story of the hell that healthcare workers and patients have gone through as a result of the fire. How units like obstetrics and Psychiatry have really struggled over the last 18 months. Now things are starting to turnaround but not really because of the department of health- their response has been appalling. Its thanks to the Development bank, Gift of the givers and the solidarity fund that the hospital is being rebuilt, but its not going to be quick. But the fire at this hospital is just one in a long line of disasters, graft and death at Gauteng Health.
metadata.Further information: RUNNING THE GAUNTLET Meanwhile parking and security are a nightmare. Doctors tell of parking chaos, and walking for miles to get to work. They have had their cars stolen, and been mugged on their way to work. Many have left ,says Professor Adam Mohamed, either for private practice or overseas. The doctors speak of a humanitarian crisis, as people with no voice died in their homes as one of the biggest public health facilities on the continent, reeled from the effects of the blaze. Gauteng Health is on fire and at times quite literally as section 27’s Sasha Stevenson delivered shows in a searing presentation of how disaster seems to court Gauteng Health. From the days of Brian Hlonwane whose friend allegedly won tenders worth R1.2 billion rand between 2006 and 2010. Hlongwane only resigned under pressure but was elected to the provincial ANC PEC even after Section 27 made the SIU report on his malfeasance public. Then came the Life Esidemeni tragedy – described by Deputy Chief Justice Dikgang Moseneke as “ a harrowing account of the death, torture and disappearance of utterly vulnerable mental health care users, in the care of an admittedly delinquent provincial government” Then in 2018 a blaze in the upper floors of Gauteng health destroyed legal documents. But it didn’t end there, as the Covid pandemic hit, Gauteng health placed orders for PPE at a cost of more than R500 million rand above market related prices. Then two fires in 2021 hit Gauteng Health. First the fire in April at Charlotte Maxeke and another also PPE related in Carletonville that destroyed R16.5 million rands worth of equipment which was being stored for the AngloGold Ashanti Hospital and R3.8 million worth of PPE. In between the blazes the hero health workers kept going to work. People like Dr Tim De Maayer who went public when he couldn’t take it anymore and made the devastating statement that “Children are dying and the horrendous conditions in our public hospitals are contributing to their deaths.” For his trouble, he was almost fired and only under pressure, was he able to keep his job. Now Doctors have their heads down and are loathe to speak out. Hardly surprising when whistleblowing regarding Gauteng Health can get you assassinated. Doctors whisper Babita Deokoran’s name in hushed tones and apologize for their absence of courage to speak out. Carte Blanche speaks to Professor Adam Mohamed, goes on a tour of the burnt hospital and asks pertinent questions of the Department of health and their response to the blaze and takes our viewers through the SAPS forensic report on the fire. We also speak to Mark Heywood formally of Section 27.
